# SB-1013 Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-RR01

Hazard description
------------------

Background: Abrasive blasting operations adjacent to or on the Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill produce airborne dust containing ferrous particles, abrasive media residue, and adhesion-promoter residues. These airborne dusts can create inhalation hazards, impair visibility at workstation interfaces, contaminate nearby controls and sensors, and increase the risk of mechanical entrapment when dust accumulates in moving assemblies. Airborne dust also degrades housekeeping and can carry combustible fines that increase fire potential in enclosed housings.

Observed pathway: Dust generated during blasting becomes aerosolized and migrates on airflow currents into the roll and mandrel enclosures, bearing housings, drive couplings, and inspection access points on the rolling mill. Migration into these areas increases wear, can mask pre-failure indicators, and can compromise seals. Field reports identified progressive buildup on local control enclosures and on mechanical linkages. Recent maintenance troubleshooting noted that unexpected sensor faults and premature wear were present where blasting had occurred without sufficient controls.

Confirmation: The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) is 430 N·m. Dust ingress can interfere with clamped interface cleanliness and may contribute to loosened fastener seating and accelerated fatigue when assemblies are not cleaned and inspected following nearby blasting activities.

Affected equipment
------------------

Primary affected equipment: Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) and all ancillary fixtures and housings on line P2-L1. Specific affected elements include mandrel assemblies, clamp bolts, bearing housings, drive couplings, local control cabinets, and inspection ports adjacent to blasting work zones.

Adjacent equipment: Any tooling, material handling fixtures, or inspection jigs located within airflow distance downwind of blasting operations on P2-L1. Maintenance and inspection activities documented in MM-P2-L1-RR01 should be reviewed for overlap and coordination with blasting operations.

Personnel at risk: Mill operators, maintenance technicians, blasting contractors, and inspection staff assigned to P2-L1. Respiratory protection and visibility impairments can affect safe task execution.

Required controls
-----------------

Objective: Prevent airborne dust migration into critical mill assemblies and reduce exposure for personnel working on or near EQ-P2-L1-RR01.

Administrative controls
- Pre-job coordination: All blasting tasks that could affect P2-L1 line areas must be scheduled and coordinated with the mill lead and maintenance planner and recorded per SOP-P2-L1-05. Notify affected shift crews prior to blasting.
- Permit-to-work: Issue a blasting notice and isolation permit that documents the area of influence and control measures. Reference MM-P2-L1-RR01 for maintenance integration and SB-1030 for related airborne hazard guidance.
- Stop work criteria: If visible dust is observed inside any control cabinet, bearing housing vent, or mandrel access port, suspend blasting-related operations until containment is re-established and affected enclosures are cleaned and inspected.

Engineering controls
- Local containment: Use localized containment enclosures or shrouds around blasting locations to capture dust at the source. Employ extraction with HEPA-rated filtration where feasible to reduce migration.
- Negative pressure and filtration: Maintain negative pressure within blasting enclosures to pull dust into filtration units rather than allowing it to migrate toward the mill. Ensure exhaust is routed away from EQ-P2-L1-RR01 intake paths.
- Sealing of vulnerable housings: Prior to blasting, temporarily seal control cabinets, inspection ports, and exposed bearing vents on EQ-P2-L1-RR01 with approved covers designed for the environment. Remove seals only after documented cleaning and inspection.

Work practices and PPE
- Cleaning prior to restart: After any blasting task in the vicinity, perform a documented cleaning of external mill housings, clamp faces, mandrel interfaces, and fastener seating areas before restoring normal operation. Use HEPA-filtered vacuums and approved wipe solvents as specified in SOP-P2-L1-05.
- Inspection of torque-critical fasteners: Following cleaning, perform visual and tactile inspection of clamp bolts and seating areas. Verify seating integrity per maintenance procedures. The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) is 430 N·m; ensure that the clamp joint is free of abrasive residue prior to any torque verification to avoid false readings or damage.
- PPE: Blasting personnel must use respiratory protection and eye protection appropriate to blasting media and particle size. Mill and maintenance personnel entering recently blasted areas should follow decontamination and respiratory guidance in SB-1030.

Step rationale and examples
- Rationale for sealing and filtration: Containment and filtered extraction remove the primary vector for dust migration. Example: when a localized extraction shroud was deployed for a comparable operation on another line, visible deposition on adjacent housings decreased and sensor fault rates dropped.
- Rationale for cleaning prior to torque verification: Abrasive residue between clamped faces or under bolt heads can create false preload conditions and permit micro-movements that lead to loosening. Cleaning restores proper seating so that torque values reflect actual clamp load.
- Rationale for coordination with maintenance: Aligning blasting with planned maintenance windows reduces the likelihood of exposing assemblies that are in-service and reduces rework.

Records to keep
----------------

Maintain the following records for audit and follow-up:
- Blasting notification and permit records as filed under SOP-P2-L1-05.
- Pre- and post-blast inspection checklists and photographs documenting seals, cleaning, and areas cleaned adjacent to EQ-P2-L1-RR01.
- Maintenance follow-up entries in MM-P2-L1-RR01 referencing any corrective actions taken due to dust ingress or discoveries during post-blast inspection.
- Torque verification and fastener inspection reports referencing the mandrel clamp bolt torque statement for EQ-P2-L1-RR01.

Effective date
--------------

Effective date: Rev E

Related documents
-----------------

See MM-P2-L1-RR01, SB-1030, SOP-P2-L1-05 for procedures and integration details.
